title: Chicken Tikka Kebabs
description: These Chicken Tika Kebabs are a diabetes-friendly way to enjoy perfectly spiced Indian food without a lot of calories or carbs.
ingredients: 1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cut into 1-inch cubes)
1 large red bell pepper (cut into 1-inch pieces)
steps: In a large bowl stir the garlic, yogurt, lemon zest and juice, spices, and kosher salt until combined.
Add the chicken to the bowl and stir until all the cubes are evenly coated in the marinade. Cover and allow to marinate for 20 minutes (or place in the fridge for up to 24 hours).
Discard the marinade and thread the chicken onto the skewers, alternating with the bell pepper and onion.

Lightly grease the grill, grill pan, or griddle and place on high heat. Once hot, place the skewers on the grill, rotating to ensure even cooking, for 12–15 minutes depending on the thickness of your chicken.
Allow the kebabs to rest, covered, for 5 minutes before serving with tzatziki sauce

title: Crock Pot Moo Shu Chicken
description: Here’s a super simple crock pot recipe that cooks while you’re out and ready for you when it’s dinner time!
ingredients: 1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (thinly sliced)
steps: Layer the slaw mix and carrots in the bottom of crockpot. Top with the chicken.
In a small bowl, mix the hoisin sauce, water, garlic, soy sauce, and cornstarch. Pour over the chicken mixture and set the crockpot to high for 4-6 hours.
Serve 1 1/2 cups of the mixture in each lettuce leaf.

title: Slow Cooker Braised Beef with Carrots and Turnips
description: Tender and moist, this Slow Cooker Braised Beef with Carrots and Turnips will be a hit with whoever eats it. Try serving this for your next Sunday family dinner!
ingredients: 1 1/2 lbs beef roast, bottom round, lean, ⅛” trim, boneless (trimmed of fat)
steps: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Brown the beef chunks on all sides. Transfer the browned beef to the slow cooker.
In the same skillet, add the remaining tablespoon of oil if needed. Sauté the onions and garlic until softened.
Deglaze the skillet with water, scraping up any browned bits. Add tomato paste and stir to combine.
Transfer the onion and tomato mixture to the slow cooker.
Add carrots, turnips, dried thyme, bay leaves, salt and pepper to the slow cooker.
Pour the low sodium tomato sauce and the beef broth over the ingredients in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 6–8 hours or until the beef is tender.
Before serving, discard bay leaves and adjust the seasoning if necessary.

title: Grilled Scallops with Chunky Salsa Verde
description: This is a great seafood dish low in fat and sodium, but is packed with protein. Try pairing it with a simple arugula salad topped with a few pieces of strawberries to balance out the spicy kick of the salsa verde.
ingredients: 1/2 lbs tomatillo (husked, rinsed, cut into small dice)
1 small jalapeño pepper (seeded, deveined and minced)
1 med zucchini (seeded, cut into a small dice)
1 tsp honey or 1/2 packet artificial sweetener
12 large scallops (tabs removed (Note: Sea scallops that are fresh or that have no preservatives added are best))
steps: Prepare an indoor or outdoor grill.
In a medium bowl, mix together the tomatillo, jalapeno, cilantro, zucchini, lime juice, Stevia and garlic. Mix together and set aside.
Pat the scallops dry with a paper towel. Toss them with the olive oil, salt and pepper in a medium bowl.
Place scallops on grill, flat side down. Turning occasionally, grill until lightly charred and just cooked through, about 2 minutes per side. Serve scallops topped with the chunky salsa verde.

title: Slow-Roasted Citrus Cod
description: White fish, like cod, has a delicate flavor which allows it to absorb the flavors of the ingredients it is cooked with. Roasting this with lemon and orange slices and fennel gives this fish a bright, citrusy flavor.
ingredients: 1 lbs cod filets (4 fillets, about 4 oz each)
1/2 small jalapeño pepper (halved, seeded, and thinly sliced)
1 med lemon (unpeeled, thinly sliced, seeds removed)
1 med orange (unpeeled, thinly sliced, seeds removed)
steps: Preheat the oven to 300°F. Toss together the fennel, orange and lemon slices, and jalapeño pepper in a 9-by-13-inch baking pan.
Lay the cod pieces next to the citrus mixture. Scatter the thyme sprigs over the fish. Drizzle with the olive oil and sprinkle with the salt and pepper.
Roast the fish for 25 to 30 minutes, or until it is opaque and cooked through. Serve the fish with the roasted fennel and citrus.

title: Budget-Friendly Vegetable Stew with Whole Wheat Dumplings
description: What’s better during the fall than a warm, tasty soup? This budget-friendly recipe is fairly easy.
ingredients: 4 cup kale (chopped, 1 bunch stemmed and chopped)
steps: Add oil to a large soup pot over medium-high heat.

Add fennel, onion and celery to oil and sauté until onions turn clear (around 4-5 minutes). Add butternut squash, sage, chicken broth, water, 1 tsp salt (optional), 1/2 tsp black pepper and bay leaves. Bring to a boil and reduce to a simmer.
Simmer stew for 20 minutes, then add kale and simmer 10 more minutes.
While stew is simmering, whisk together all dumpling ingredients to form a stiff batter. Set aside.
After kale simmers for 10 minutes remove bay leaf.

Use a 1/4 cup measure to scoop dumplings on top of stew to make 8 dumplings. Do not stir once dumplings have been added to the top of the stew. Cover and reduce to a low simmer for 10 minutes until dumplings are cooked through and puffed.

title: Orange and Walnut Salad
description: Serve this light salad as a healthy option at your holiday gathering this year. It’ll provide you with some fresh fruit and veggies – two things that are often missing from the typical holiday spread!
serving_size: about 2/3 cup orange-carrot mixture + 1 cup greens
steps: Place the greens on a platter. Top with the carrots, onion, and oranges.
For the vinaigrette, whisk together the orange and lemon juices, honey, and mustard. Slowly add the oil in a thin stream, whisking constantly.
Drizzle the vinaigrette over the salad. Add pepper to taste, and top with the walnuts.

title: Budget-Friendly Summer Vegetable Frittata
description: This frittata is a great way to get more veggies into your day and can be enjoyed for brunch or dinner. By using a combination of egg whites and whole eggs, you cut back on some of the saturated fat and cholesterol.
ingredients: 1 med red bell pepper (seeded and diced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Add olive oil to an oven safe, non-stick, sauté pan over medium high heat.
Add mushrooms and sauté until all of the liquid from the mushrooms is evaporated.
Add bell pepper, onion and spinach and sauté until vegetables are softened and liquid is evaporated.
Whisk eggs, egg whites, milk, salt (optional), pepper, cayenne pepper and basil in a medium bowl. Pour over vegetables and stir until eggs start to set.
Smooth the top of the frittata with a spatula, and put in oven to bake for 20 minutes or until eggs are set.
Slide the frittata out of the pan onto a plate and slice into 8 pie slices.

title: Pomegranate Raspberry Smoothie Bowl
description: Silken tofu makes a creamy base filled with protein and healthy fats in this morning smoothie bowl. Topped with pomegranate seeds and muesli, a healthy whole grain and dried fruit cereal, this smoothie bowl will fill you up and keep you going all morning. This is a vegan, vegetarian and low-fat recipe.
steps: Place the tofu, pomegranate juice, raspberries, and syrup in a blender or food processor. Blend on high until creamy and pink in color.
Divide the mix between 2 bowls. Top each with half the pomegranate seeds and 2 tablespoons muesli.

title: Ensalada de atún asiática
description: ¡Esta ensalada de atún asiática es perfecta para los amantes de la gastronomía que buscan un plato principal saludable con un toque asiático!
serving_size: 1,5 tazas de ensalada con poco menos de 113 gramos de pescado.
ingredients: 2 tbsp salsa de soja baja en sodio o reducida en sodio
2 1/2 tbsp sustituto del azúcar moreno bajo en calorías
6 taza lechuga mixta de primavera (Lavado y secado (o centrifugado en una centrifugadora de ensaladas))
1 med pepino(s) (sembrado y cortado en juliana)
1/4 taza vinagre de vino de arroz
steps: Precalienta una parrilla, ya sea de interior o de exterior.
En un tazón pequeño, bate la salsa de soya, el sustituto de azúcar moreno, la salsa picante (opcional) y la pimienta negra. Reserva.
Rocíe la parrilla de interior con aceite en aerosol. Si usa una parrilla de exterior, asegúrese de que las rejillas estén limpias y ligeramente engrasadas.

Unta el atún y los espárragos con la marinada de salsa de soja. Colócalos en la parrilla. Asa el atún durante 3 minutos por cada lado. Asa los espárragos, dándoles la vuelta con frecuencia, hasta que empiecen a ablandarse (unos 6-8 minutos). Retira el atún y los espárragos de la parrilla, espolvorea con semillas de sésamo y déjalos enfriar. El atún debe estar ligeramente rosado en el centro, pero no crudo.
Mezcla la lechuga, el pimiento rojo y el pepino en una ensaladera.
En un tazón pequeño, bate los ingredientes del aderezo. Viértelo sobre la ensalada y mezcla suavemente para que se impregne bien. Divide la ensalada en partes iguales en cuatro platos.

Una vez que el atún y los espárragos se hayan enfriado a temperatura ambiente o ligeramente más, corta el atún en rodajas y distribúyelo equitativamente entre las cuatro ensaladas (un poco menos de 115 gramos de atún por ensalada). Colócalo con cuidado sobre la ensalada.
Corta los espárragos por la mitad y colócalos alrededor del borde de la ensalada.

title: 5-Ingredient Blueberry Protein Muffins
description: Don’t be deceived. These 5 Ingredient Blueberry Protein Muffins may be smaller in size, but they sure are delicious! This recipe can help fit more protein into your diet by combining fresh, sweet-tart blueberries with the warm flavors of almond butter and vanilla Greek nonfat yogurt. Better yet, this recipe contains just five ingredients meaning it’s oh-so-easy to make—and take on the go.
steps: Preheat oven to 375˚F. Spray 6 muffin cups with cooking spray. In large bowl, stir together banana, quinoa, nonfat yogurt and almond butter until blended. Fold in blueberries.
Spoon batter into prepared muffin cups. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown and set in center. Let cool completely.

title: Pulled Chicken with Cilantro Lime
description: Cooking chicken breasts in a slow cooker tenderizes the chicken breast making it easy to pull apart and shredded. This chicken is infused with a spicy lime flavor and is delicious on lettuce leaves or in a tortilla with a side of guacamole and salsa.
ingredients: 1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (all fat discarded)
1 small lime (cut into wedges for serving)
steps: In a medium bowl, stir together the onion, lime juice, and salt. Cover with plastic wrap and set aside at room temperature for 3 to 5 hours, while the chicken cooks.

Place the chicken in a medium slow cooker. Sprinkle with the chili powder and cumin. Pour the chicken broth around the chicken. Cover and cook on low for 3 to 5 hours or until chicken reaches a temperature of 165°F.

Remove the chicken from the slow cooker and using the tines of two forks, shred the chicken. Place the chicken in a bowl and toss with the onion lime mixture. Serve with lime wedges and chopped cilantro sprinkled on top.

Electric pressure cooker variation: Prepare the onion lime mixture as above. Place the chicken in the pressure cooker. Sprinkle with chili powder and cumin. Pour the chicken broth around the chicken. Secure the lid. Cook on high pressure for 6 minutes. Allow the pressure to release naturally for 5 minutes, then quickly release the remaining pressure. Proceed as above.

title: Quick Broccoli Slaw
description: This crunch side dish is a twist on traditional tangy-sweet broccoli salad, but with no added sugar.
steps: In a salad bowl, mix together the broccoli slaw, raisins, and turkey bacon.
In a small bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, yogurt, and vinegar. Pour the dressing over the salad and toss to coat.

title: Tofu Stir Fry
description: Here’s a super quick vegetarian dinner to share with your family. Never cooked with tofu? This recipe is a great place to start!
ingredients: 1 lbs extra firm tofu (drained and cut into 1-inch chunks)
1/4 cup lite sesame ginger salad dressing
4 stalks green onion (scallion) ((white and green parts), thinly sliced)
steps: Mix the tofu and sesame ginger salad dressing in a bowl and marinate for 30 minutes.
Once the tofu is done marinating, remove the tofu from the marinade and reserve the marinade.
Add the sesame oil and cooking spray to a wok or large sauté pan over high heat. Add the tofu and stir fry for 7-8 minutes, or until the tofu is golden brown.
Add the broccoli and mushrooms, and stir fry for 3-4 minutes. Add in the scallions and almonds, and stir fry for an additional 2 minutes.

In a bowl or cup, whisk together the vegetable broth, cornstarch, soy sauce, hot sauce, brown sugar substitute, and garlic. Whisk in the reserved sesame ginger dressing marinade. Pour the mixture over the tofu and bring to a boil.
Reduce to a simmer and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve Suggestion: Serve over brown rice or in lettuce cups

title: Grilled Zucchini
description: This grilled zucchini is a quick side dish that is simple, fresh, and full of flavor.
steps: Preheat the grill or a grill pan to 350 degrees.
In a large bowl, toss the zucchini rounds with olive oil, dried thyme, salt, and pepper.
Use tongs to place the rounds on the grill.
Grill for 3–4 minutes on each side, until tender and charred in places.

title: Socca with Poached Eggs, Roasted Tomatoes, and Fresh Basil
description: Socca, also known as farinata, is a thin chickpea flour pancake commonly found in both Italian and French cuisines. In this recipe, Katie Cavuto tops wedges of the warm chickpea crepe with roasted tomatoes, poached eggs, and fresh basil. For an easy, make-ahead brunch or weekday breakfast, make the batter and poach the eggs the night before. To store the poached eggs overnight, plunge them into an airtight container filled with cold water and place them in the fridge.
serving_size: 1 slice of socca +1 poached egg + 2 tbsp roasted tomatoes + 2 tbsp basil
steps: Place a 10-inch cast-iron skillet about 12 inches from your oven’s heating element and set the oven to “Broil.”

In a small bowl, whisk together chickpea flour, cumin, and salt. Slowly stream in water, whisking quickly to eliminate lumps, then stir in 1 tablespoon of the olive oil. Cover the bowl and set aside for at least 15 minutes. (Or store it in the refrigerator for up to 12 hours.) The batter should be a thin, pancake batter–like consistency.

After the batter has rested, carefully remove the hot skillet from the oven. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the skillet and pour in the socca batter. Broil for 8–10 minutes, or until the edges of the socca are browned and the center is set.

Meanwhile, set a metal strainer in the bottom of a large pot, fill the pot 2/3 full with water, and add the vinegar. Crack each egg into a small prep bowl. Place the pot over medium-high heat and bring the vinegar and water to a simmer. Using a long-handled spoon, stir the water in a wide, circular motion to create a whirlpool. Quickly, while the whirlpool is still going, slide in the eggs, one by one. Once all the eggs are in the water, poach them without stirring until the whites are set and the yolks are no longer runny, about 4–6 minutes. Using tongs, carefully lift the strainer out of the water with the eggs.

Remove socca from the oven and cut it into 8 wedges. To serve, place a socca wedge on each of 8 plates and top each serving with 1 poached egg, 2 tablespoons roasted tomatoes, and 2 tablespoons chopped basil. Season servings with pepper.

title: Shrimp Paella with Cauliflower Rice
description: This shrimp paella is full of flavor from sausage, bell peppers, turmeric and paprika. Using riced cauliflower makes this a lower carb alternative to a traditional Spanish paella.
ingredients: 1 med red bell pepper (seeded and diced)
1 (3-oz) link fully cooked adouille or chorizo chicken sausage (diced)
6 cup fresh or frozen cauliflower rice
steps: Add cooking spray to a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage, onion, bell pepper and garlic. Sauté until onions are starting to caramelize, about 8 minutes.
Stir in turmeric and paprika. Add the broth, cauliflower rice, salt and pepper. Bring to boil then reduce heat to low, cover and simmer about 5 minutes.
Add the shrimp to the pan, then cover and cook until shrimp are just opaque in center, about 6 minutes.

title: BBQ Chicken Pizza
description: Serve this pizza with a big garden salad drizzled lightly with low-fat Ranch dressing. It’s a quick, easy and budget-friendly meal!
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Spray a baking sheet with cooking spray.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper on both sides.
Place the chicken on the prepared baking sheet and bake for 25 minutes or until the juices run clear. Remove the chicken from the oven and chop into half-inch pieces.
In a small saucepan, combine the sugar-free apricot preserves, barbeque sauce, and hot sauce. Bring to a boil.
Spoon the sauce over the pizza crust. Top the crust with cooked chicken, sliced onion, carrot, and cheese. Sprinkle the cheese with the dried oregano.
Bake the pizza for 20-25 minutes or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.

title: Banana, medium
description: Nutrition information for a banana

title: Onion, Shallot and Herb Frittata
description: Looking for a light and simple breakfast to enjoy with the family during the holidays? This frittata will do the trick. Serve it with some greens, whole wheat toast and some fruit on the side if your meal plan allows for it.
ingredients: 2 tbsp Parmesan or Romano cheese (freshly grated)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Heat 1 tsp of the olive oil in a large nonstick ovenproof skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and shallot and sauté for about 7 to 8 minutes. Remove the onion mixture from the skillet and set aside.
Beat the eggs, egg whites, basil, and salt and pepper. Fold in the onion mixture.
In the remaining 1 tsp of oil, heat the egg mixture on medium low in the skillet. Cook without stirring for about 8 minutes.
Transfer the skillet to the oven, sprinkle with the cheese, and bake for about 10 minutes until top is no longer runny. Cook an additional 5 minutes if necessary. Cut into wedges to serve.

title: Pumpkin Seeds
description: Nutrition information for pumpkin seeds

title: Garlicky Tomato Salad
description: Plum and cherry tomatoes taste good year-round, so you can enjoy this salad anytime. In the summer, feel free to substitute yellow or heirloom tomatoes. Grilled shrimp is superb in this salad, so add it if you want to turn this into a main dish. Try this with sliced mint leaves in place of the basil or use half mint and half basil.
ingredients: 1 head butter lettuce (large leaves torn into smaller pieces)
steps: Place a layer of lettuce leaves on a serving platter or on four plates and arrange the sliced tomatoes. Place the cherry tomatoes on top.
Whisk together the garlic, vinegar, mustard, oil, salt, and pepper and pour over the tomatoes.
Scatter the basil leaves and the pumpkin and sunflower seeds over the tomatoes and serve at once.

title: Air Fryer Buttermilk Fried Chicken
description:
Is it possible to make fried chicken diabetes-friendly? Absolutely! Especially if you have an air fryer. This small appliance "fries" food with hot circulating air, so you can create the crispy, crunchy exterior or frying with a fraction of the fat and calories from traditional deep frying. This recipe creates juicy, flavorful fried chicken by marinating the chicken in buttermilk, then coating it in a cornflake crust. Then the air fryer works its magic and delivers this fried chicken that's crispy, tender, and loaded with flavor! Top this chicken with a reduced-fat Creamy Gravy and pair with a side of Southern Collard Greens for the ultimate southern comfort meal!

Looking for more diabetes-friendly air fryer recipes? Check out this article.

Powered by Homemade
ingredients: 1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cut in half lengthwise to make 4 equal portions)
steps: In a small, deep bowl, stir together the buttermilk and hot sauce. Place the chicken in the buttermilk mixture. Allow to stand 15 minutes.

Place the cornflakes into the work bowl of a food processor. Process until coarse crumbs form. Add the cornmeal, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper and pulse until evenly mixed. Pour the crumbs into a shallow bowl. (if you don't have a food processor, you can crush the cornflakes in a plastic bag with a rolling pin.)
Drain the chicken, allowing the excess buttermilk to drip back into bowl. Coat the chicken pieces evenly in the cornflake mixture. Place the coated chicken pieces on a wire rack.

Place the chicken in the air fryer basket. Spray with nonstick cooking spray for 2 seconds (do not crowd the chicken; cook in batches if all the chicken doesn't fit). Set the temperature to 375°F and air fry for 7 minutes.
Turn the chicken pieces. Air fry for an additional 7–10 minutes or until the chicken is done and a meat thermometer inserted in the center registers 165°F.

title: Tilapia Stew with Green Peppers
description: Stewed tomatoes make this fish stew and easy and flavorful seafood dinner. Poaching fish in a sauce made with tomatoes keeps the fish tender.
ingredients: 1 can can stewed tomatoes with Italian seasonings (14.5 ounces)
1 lbs tilapia (rinsed and cut into 1-inch pieces)
steps: Place a large saucepan over medium heat until hot. Coat the pan with nonstick cooking spray, add the bell pepper, and cook 5 minutes or until beginning to lightly brown, stirring frequently.

Add the tomatoes and water, increase to high heat, and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat, cover tightly, and simmer until the tomatoes are tender. Using the back of a spoon, break up the larger pieces of tomato.

Add the fish and seasonings and stir very gently. Increase the heat to high and bring just to a boil. Reduce the heat, cover tightly, and simmer 3 minutes or until the fish is opaque in the center. Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, 10 minutes to develop flavors.

title: Black Bean & Quinoa Mason Jar Salad
description: This salad is a fresh, low-fat, Mediterranean-style, vegetarian, and vegan recipe that can be a make-ahead meal. Packed with plant-based protein, fiber, and veggies, and layered with a zesty lime-cilantro vinaigrette, it’s perfect for grab-and-go lunches that help with managing blood glucose (blood sugar). With no added sugars and high fiber carbs that will digest more slowly, it’s a smart, satisfying option for people with diabetes.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cup canned low sodium black beans (drained and rinsed)
steps: Rinse quinoa under cold water. Combine with 2 cups of water in a pot and bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer until water is absorbed, about 15 minutes. Let cool.
In a small bowl or jar, whisk together the lime juice, olive oil, Dijon mustard, garlic, cilantro, salt, and pepper.
Assemble salads. In each large mason jar or tall container, in this order, combine: 2–3 Tbsp vinaigrette
Sprinkle of red onion
1/2 cup black beans
1/2 cup cooked quinoa
1/4 cup each of tomato, cucumber, and bell pepper
Small handful chopped spinach

title: Deviled Eggs
description: Deviled eggs are a classic appetizer. They’re a quick and easy choice for any holiday party or weekend get-together.
steps: Place the eggs in a small saucepan so that they won’t bounce or move around and crack. Cover with water. Bring to a boil. Immediately turn off and cover. Let sit for 15-18 minutes to continue cooking. Pour out the hot water. Shake the eggs in the pan to crack the shells. Add cold water and let sit. (This will make them easier to peel.)

Peel the eggs and cut them in half vertically. Remove yolks, place them in a small bowl, and mash with a fork. Add mayo, mustard, salt and pepper. Fill egg whites with mixture. Garnish with sliced grape tomatoes, sliced olives, sliced radishes, sliced scallions, or a drop of caviar or truffle paste. (Garnishes are optional.)

title: Simple Tuna & Tomato Salad Stack
description: This quick, no-cook tuna salad pairs creamy mayonnaise with tender canned tuna and fresh tomato slices for a light, satisfying single-serve meal or snack. It’s simple, clean, and ready in minutes.
steps: Drain the 1/2 cup canned tuna and place it in a small bowl.
Add 1 tablespoon mayonnaise and mix until the tuna is evenly coated.
Arrange the 2 tomato slices on a plate.
Spoon the tuna mixture on top of the tomato slices or serve alongside them.
Enjoy immediately.

title: Tomato and Peach Salad
description: This salad is perfect for late summer when peaches and tomatoes are at their peak.
ingredients: 3 med peaches (pitted and cut into thick wedges)
steps: In a large bowl, combine the peaches, tomatoes, cherry tomatoes, and red onion, and gently toss.
In a small bowl or measuring cup, whisk together the vinegar, lemon juice, and honey. Slowly add the oil in a thin stream, whisking to emulsify. Add the salt and black pepper.
Add the dressing to the peaches and tomatoes, and gently toss. Fold in the mint leaves. To serve, turn out the salad onto a large platter.

title: Just Peachy Bowls
description: These gorgeous “bowls” look so impressive, but they’re really easy to prepare. You’ll actually be making your own flavored greek yogurt, which is the best way to create the flavor and sweetness level just right for you. When dolloped over juicy peaches, the result is simply divine—especially when the fruit is at its peak in the spring or summer. Grilling the peaches makes this dessert uniquely sweet and smoky, but if you're looking for an even quicker dessert, you can skip the grill and leave the peaches raw.
ingredients: 2 large peaches (fully ripened, halved, pits and stems removed)
2 tbsp natural sliced almonds pan-toasted, or roasted pistachios
steps: In a small bowl, stir together the yogurt, honey, and vanilla.
Spritz the cut side of peach halves with cooking spray and place the peaches cut-side-down on a hot grill. Grill until grill marks start to form, and the peaches are heated through, 2-3 minutes.
Place each peach half onto a small plate, cut-side up. Top each half with the yogurt mixture, almonds, and mint, and serve.

title: Roasted Veggie Quinoa Bowl
description: This Roasted Veggie Quinoa Bowl is a satisfying delight, easy enough to put together for lunch or dinner. Make it colorful by adding your favorite veggies to the mix. Serve with fresh lemon wedges for a burst of citrus flavor.
serving_size: ½ cup cooked quinoa + 3 oz chicken + 1 cup veggies + ½ Tbsp feta
ingredients: 4 cup mixed, nonstarchy vegetables (bell peppers, cherry tomatoes, zucchini, broccoli, etc.)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
In a saucepan, combine the dry quinoa with 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until quinoa is cooked and water is absorbed.
While the quinoa is cooking, spread the cubed chicken and chopped vegetables on a baking sheet.
Drizzle olive oil over the chicken and vegetables, sprinkle with the dried oregano, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Roast the chicken and vegetables in the preheated oven for about 20–25 minutes or until they are tender and slightly browned and the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165 degrees F.
Assemble by dividing the cooked quinoa and roasted vegetable mix among bowls.
Top with crumbled feta cheese and serve with fresh lemon wedges.

title: Hearty Breakfast Frittata
description: Frittatas are a great way to use up extra vegetables before they go bad. Using whatever you have on hand, a variety of non-starchy vegetables helps keep the carb content low and feelings of fullness high.
ingredients: 2 cup kale (chopped, cut into small pieces)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Spray an 8- x 8-inch baking pan with cooking spray.
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs and egg substitute until well combined. Add in cottage cheese and yogurt and whisk to combine. Set aside.
In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add onion and red pepper and sauté for 3 minutes, until vegetables begin to soften. Add garlic and sauté for another minute.
Stir in spinach, kale, and broccoli, and cook to wilt the greens, about 2 minutes. Add the artichokes, red pepper flakes, and dried basil. Remove from heat.
Spread the vegetables in the bottom of the prepared pan. Pour the egg and cheese mixture over the vegetables and make sure they are covered well.
Place the pan in the middle of the oven and bake for 40–45 minutes, or until the mixture is set and doesn’t jiggle when lightly shaken.
Allow to cool for 10 minutes, then cut into 6 pieces. Garnish with fresh basil if desired.

title: Mediterranean Breakfast Pita Panini
description: A whole grain pita pocket filled with cheesy eggs, sundried tomatoes, and spinach makes this panini a delicious and healthy option.
ingredients: 1 whole whole grain pita bread (cut in half)
2 tbsp oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes (drained and chopped)
steps: Spray a nonstick pan with cooking spray and heat over medium heat. Whisk in the egg and egg substitute and cook until partially firm. Stir in the cottage cheese, tomatoes, basil, pepper, and garlic powder. Continue cooking until the eggs are cooked.
Place half the mozzarella cheese on the inside of half of the pita. Lay half the spinach leaves on top and fill the pita with half the egg mixture. Repeat with the second pita.

Heat a grill pan or skillet over medium heat. Spray lightly with cooking spray and place the stuffed pitas, cheese side down, on the pan once hot. Allow to cook until browned and cheese has melted. Turn the pita over and cook until the other side is browned.

title: Southwestern Coleslaw
description: Fresh coleslaw with a southwestern zip. Toasted pecans add a delicate crunch along with healthy fats along with potassium, magnesium and calcium – nutrients that are helpful with blood pressure management.
ingredients: 1 med red bell pepper (seeded, cored, and diced)
1 head green cabbage (outer leaves removed, shredded)
steps: In a large salad bowl, combine the cabbage, carrots, red pepper, scallions, and jalapeño pepper and toss well.

In a small bowl, whisk together the vinegar, lime juice, honey, and chipotle seasoning. Add the olive oil in a thin stream, whisking to emulsify. Pour the dressing on the cabbage mixture and mix well. Garnish the coleslaw with the toasted pecans.

title: Low-Carb Artichoke Chicken Wraps
description: These are a great make-ahead item for your lunchbox.
ingredients: 1/2 cup artichoke hearts (chopped, drained and rinsed)
steps: Whisk the egg, egg white, and milk until well combined and slightly frothy. Sift the coconut flour into the mixture and whisk again until well combined. Let the batter rest at room temperature for 15 minutes.
While the wrap batter is resting, toss together the chicken, artichoke hearts, red onion, baby spinach, and Italian dressing. Keep the filling refrigerated until needed.
Add the cooking spray to a 10-inch nonstick sauté pan over medium heat. Let the pan heat until a drop of water sizzles in the bottom of the pan.

Re-whisk the wrap batter and then pour 1/4 cup of the wrap batter to thinly coat the bottom of the pan (add a little more if needed to coat the bottom of the pan). Let the wrap cook until the edges begin to brown. Using a spatula, flip the wrap and continue to cook for another minute. Slide the wrap on to a plate and continue this process to make 6 “wraps” or crepes. Let the wraps cool.
Divide the chicken mixture evenly among each wrap (about 1/2 cup of filling per wrap) and roll.

title: Strawberry-Lemon Cheesecake
description: This upside down cheesecake is a fun way to enjoy all the flavors of cheesecake with fewer calories, sugar and fat. If you can't find fat-free ricotta cheese you can substitute cottage cheese.
steps: In a small bowl, mix together the ricotta cheese, honey, lemon zest, and cinnamon.
Divide the mixture among four individual dessert dishes. Top each dish with a portion of strawberries and sprinkle with some of the graham cracker crumbs.

title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Chipotle Aioli
description: Roasted Brussels sprouts accompanied by a smoky chipotle aioli make for a bold, diabetes-friendly side dish. Pair it with a simple lean protein like grilled chicken breast for an easy weeknight dinner.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
Toss the halved Brussels sprouts with the olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Spread the Brussels sprouts in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 25 minutes or until the Brussels sprouts are golden brown and crispy on the edges.
While the Brussels sprouts are roasting, prepare the aioli.
In a small bowl, combine the mayo, minced chipotle peppers, minced garlic, lime juice, and salt. Mix well.
Once the Brussels sprouts are roasted, transfer them to a serving dish. Serve chipotle aioli on the side.

title: Creamy Gravy
description: Creamy, pepper-seasoned gravy is a staple in southern comfort foods like biscuits and gravy and chicken fried steak. This diabetes-friendly version uses a vegetable oil-based margarine to reduce the saturated fat that's usually found in traditional gravy. Serve this with Air Fryer Buttermilk Chicken for the ultimate southern comfort meal!
steps: Melt margarine in a small saucepan over medium-high heat.
Stir in all-purpose flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly and blending until the mixture is smooth. Season with coarse ground black pepper.
Gradually blend in skim milk. Cook, stirring constantly, until mixture bubbles and thickens.

title: Easy Perfectly Cooked Lentils
description:
If you’ve never cooked lentils, now is the time to give it a try with this easy Perfectly Cooked Lentils recipe. As a legume, lentils are packed with plant-based protein and will get you satisfied and powered through your day. We show you how to cook lentils in a healthy and diabetes-friendly way.

Add in your favorite non-starchy veggies like onions and bell peppers for a deliciously satisfying meal.
steps: Rinse the lentils under cold water in a fine-mesh sieve or colander.
In a medium saucepan, combine the rinsed lentils, vegetable broth, and bay leaf (if using).
Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the saucepan with a lid, and let the lentils simmer for 20–25 minutes or until they are tender but still hold their shape.
Once cooked, remove the saucepan from the heat and discard the bay leaf.
Drain any excess liquid if necessary.

title: Cottage Cheese and Pineapple Parfait
description: Nutrition information for Cottage Cheese and Pineapple Parfait
steps: Spoon 1 cup of low-fat cottage cheese into a bowl or glass.
Add 1/2 cup diced pineapple on top.
Lightly stir if you prefer mixed flavors, or leave it layered for a parfait-style presentation.
Serve immediately.

title: Yaya’s Vegetable Paella
description: Most paellas are made with seafood or chicken, but this vegetarian version is still tasty and authentic. You can also add additional non-starchy vegetables to the mix if you want!
ingredients: 1 med green bell pepper (cut in 4 pieces)
1/2 cup fresh green beans (cut in 1/2-inch pieces (or use frozen))
steps: Heat oil in medium frying pan over medium heat. Sauté pepper and green beans for 2 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients except lima beans and artichoke hearts and bring to a boil. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer 20 minutes.
Add lima beans and artichokes, stir, cover, and cook 5 more minutes.

title: Steamed Broccoli with Crispy Garlic
description: Crispy garlic adds a deliciously modern twist to simple steamed broccoli. Delicious, low carb, and nutrient rich, broccoli makes an excellent side dish for those trying to make healthy dinner choices.
steps: Place the broccoli florets in a steamer basket over a pot of boiling water.
Steam the broccoli for 5–7 minutes or until it is tender-crisp. Remove from heat.
While the broccoli is steaming, heat 1 Tbsp olive oil in a small skillet over medium heat.
Add the thinly sliced garlic to the skillet and sauté for 1–2 minutes until it becomes golden brown and crispy. Be careful not to burn the garlic.
Remove the crispy garlic from the skillet and place it on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Place the steamed broccoli in a serving dish.
Drizzle 1 Tbsp of the olive oil over the broccoli and toss to coat.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Sprinkle the crispy garlic and sesame seeds over the steamed broccoli.

title: Cod With Avocado Corn Salsa Salad
description: Cod is a hearty white fish that picks up the flavors from the other ingredients it is paired with. The avocado and corn salsa adds a zesty southwestern flavor and beautiful color to this dish.
ingredients: 1 med avocado (ripe, peeled, seeded, and chopped)
4 whole cod filets (about 5 ounces each, rinsed and patted dry)
steps: Preheat grill or grill pan coated with cooking spray to medium-high heat.
Combine all salsa ingredients, except the avocado, in a medium bowl. Gently stir in the avocado and set aside.

Brush both sides of the fish fillets with oil and sprinkle evenly with the cumin, 1/4 teaspoon of the salt, and black pepper. Cook 4 minutes on each side or until opaque in center. Serve with salsa alongside.

title: Low-Carb Cauliflower Breadsticks
description: Enjoy the savory taste of cheesy garlic bread without all the carbs! These “bread” sticks are great on their own paired with a soup or pasta. You could also use this recipe as the base for a low carb pizza or flatbread.
ingredients: 1 cup shredded part-skim mozzarella cheese (divided use)
steps: Preheat your oven to 375°F.

Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper and spray with cooking spray. Pour on the riced cauliflower and spread into an even layer. Bake for 15 minutes. Remove cauliflower from the oven, and turn the temperature up to 450°F.
Line a large bowl with two layers of paper towels or a clean dish towel. Pour in the cooked cauliflower and let it cool.
Add another layer of towels on top of the cooled cauliflower and press down with your hands. Squeeze out as much liquid as you can.
In a large mixing bowl, mix the cauliflower, egg whites, 1/2 cup of cheese, garlic powder, herbs and pepper.

Line your baking sheet with a fresh layer of parchment paper. Spray with cooking spray. Place your cauliflower dough on the prepared baking sheet and press into an even rectangle about 1/4” thick and 7x9” in size. Bake for 20 minutes, then sprinkle the rest of the cheese on top. Broil a couple more minutes until the cheese melts and starts to brown.
Let cool, then cut into 12 breadsticks.

title: Buffalo Tempeh "Wings"
description: These vegetarian and low carb buffalo tempeh "wings" are a bold, plant-based alternative to the classic appetizer, with all the heat and tang of traditional wings—minus the saturated fat. Steaming and baking the tempeh creates a crispy texture, while the sugar-free sauce keeps added sugars in check. It’s a fun, high-protein option that fits well into a diabetes-conscious eating plan.
ingredients: 1/3 cup hot sauce (such as Frank's Red Hot)
1 tsp sugar-free maple-type syrup (with monk fruit)
1/4 cup light ranch dressing (creamy, with low-fat yogurt)
steps: Fill a small saucepan with 1 inch of water and bring to a simmer. Place tempeh in a steamer basket, cover, and steam for 5 minutes to soften and remove bitterness. Pat dry and transfer to a bowl.
Toss the tempeh with soy sauce, 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar, ½ tsp garlic powder, smoked paprika, and black pepper. Let sit for 5 minutes to absorb flavors.

Preheat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Sprinkle cornstarch over the tempeh and toss to coat lightly. Arrange tempeh in a single layer and bake for 20 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crisp.
In a small saucepan over low heat, combine hot sauce, 1 Tbsp vinegar, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, and ½ tsp garlic powder. Stir until warm and well blended.
Remove tempeh from the oven and toss with the warm sauce until coated. Serve with ranch for dipping and celery and carrot sticks.

title: Sheet Pan Balsamic Chicken and Brussels Sprouts
description: Sheet pan dinners are quick and easy meals without a lot of clean up. Elevate your chicken with delicious balsamic vinegar and a side of crispy brussels sprouts for the perfect and healthy weeknight dinner.
ingredients: 4 whole boneless, skinless chicken breasts (6 ounces each)
1 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped, for garnish, optional)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, whisk together balsamic vinegar, olive oil, honey, minced garlic, dried thyme, kosher salt, and black pepper to create the marinade.
Place chicken breasts in a large bowl and pour the marinade over the chicken, ensuring it's well coated.
Arrange the chicken breasts on the sheet pan and Brussels sprouts on the other.
Add the Brussels sprouts to the same bowl and coat well with the remaining marinade. Arrange the Brussel sprouts around the chicken on the sheet pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until the chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 165 degrees F, about 25–30 minutes.
Remove from the oven, let it rest for a few minutes, and then garnish with fresh parsley and lemon zest and juice, if using.

title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Bacon
description: Add this simple, low carb side dish to your favorite protein entree. Roasting enhances the flavor of Brussels sprouts, and turkey bacon adds a delicious salt, savoriness. You could use fresh or frozen Brussels sprouts here.
ingredients: 3 slice turkey bacon (extra lean, cut into 1-inch pieces)
steps: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Spray a baking sheet with cooking spray.
Place Brussels sprouts in a bowl and add oil; toss to coat.
Add remaining ingredients and mix well.
Place Brussels sprouts on a baking sheet and bake for 35-40 minutes or crisp on the outside.

title: Veggie Waffle Omelette
description: This creative waffle omelette combines egg whites, colorful veggies, and lean turkey sausage into a fun, protein-rich breakfast that skips the carbs. Cooking it in a waffle iron adds crisp edges without needing extra oil or flour. With its low saturated fat and high protein content, it’s a great option for people with diabetes looking for a satisfying start to their day. This is a low carb, very low carb, and low-fat recipe.
ingredients: 1/2 cup turkey sausage (diced, cooked [choose a lower sodium variety])
steps: Set your waffle iron to a low or medium setting and allow it to preheat. Lightly coat both the top and bottom plates with cooking spray.
Place the egg whites in a large bowl. Whisk vigorously until slightly frothy.
Add the shredded cheese, diced turkey sausage, bell peppers, onions, and black pepper to the eggs. Stir until all ingredients are evenly distributed.

Pour a portion of the egg mixture onto the center of the preheated waffle iron, ensuring not to overfill. Close the lid gently. Cook for approximately 3-5 minutes, or until the eggs are fully set and the surface is lightly golden. Cooking times may vary depending on your waffle iron; monitor closely to prevent overcooking.
Carefully remove the omelette from the waffle iron using a spatula. Repeat the process with the remaining egg mixture. Serve warm, garnished with chives.

title: Tofu Spring Rolls
description: You can also make these spring rolls with just the lettuce as wrapper instead of the rice paper to make this recipe even lower in carbohydrate.
ingredients: 6 whole spring roll wrappers (rice paper, 0.25 ounce each)
1 small cucumber(s) (peeled, seeded and thinly sliced into strips)
1 tbsp soy sauce (lower sodium, for sauce)
1/2 tsp Thai style chili garlic sauce (for sauce)
steps: Preheat oven to 475 degrees F. Coat a baking sheet with cooking spray and set aside.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce and brown sugar substitute.
Slice tofu into 6 slices. Place on the baking sheet and lightly brush each slice with the soy sauce mixture. Bake for 20 minutes. Cool completely.
Once the tofu is cool, cut each slice into three smaller slices.
Divide the mango and cucumber each into 6 equal portions.
Soak one rice paper wrapper in warm water until softened, about 30 seconds. Lay the rice paper on a clean, flat surface. Place one lettuce leaf on top of the rice paper.
Place one portion of the mango and cucumber each in the center of the rice paper. Top the vegetables with 3 small slices of tofu and two slices of avocado.
Fold the left and right sides of the wrapper and lettuces into the middle until almost touching. Roll paper from the bottom to form the roll tightly. Repeat for remaining rice papers. Set aside.
Combine the sauce ingredients in a small saucepan over high heat. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Simmer for 2 minutes. Serve warm with cold spring rolls for dipping.

title: Green Bell Pepper Enchiladas
description:
Spice up your mealtime with a delicious twist on a Mexican favorite—Green Bell Pepper Enchiladas! Whether you're a fan of Tex-Mex cuisine or looking to add some excitement to your dinner table, these enchiladas are a diabetes-friendly delight.

Cook’s tip: These can be made ahead and frozen for a quick meal later.
ingredients: 1/4 cup shredded Mexican cheese blend (reduced fat)
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F
Spray a large skillet with cooking spray and heat over medium heat. Add green peppers, jalapeño, green onion, and garlic. Cook over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, until the peppers start to soften.
Remove from heat and place in a bowl with the shredded chicken and mix. Set aside.
Return skillet to the heat and add the olive oil. Whisk in the flour for about 1 minute until smooth.
Slowly pour the chicken broth in, whisking until the sauce is thickened and smooth, about 3–4 minutes. Add the salt, coriander, and yogurt and whisk until smooth. Remove from heat.
Pour a small amount of sauce in a 10 x 8 (or medium size) baking dish. Spread to coat the bottom of the pan.

Place tortillas on a flat surface and divide the chicken and pepper mix between them, placing the mix in the center of each. Roll tightly and place seam side down in the baking dish. Pour remaining sauce over the stuffed tortillas and sprinkle with the shredded cheese.
Bake for 15–20 minutes, until the sauce is bubbling and the cheese has melted.
